newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks advance in early trade.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks advance in early trade.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks moved ahead firmly in early trade on Tuesday morning, buoyed by trends in overseas markets and high turnover levels, brokers said.
"The Hong Kong market is going to continue in its bull phase and probably test the 12,600 level this week or next week," said Peter Lai, associate director at OCBC Securities.
The Hang Seng Index put on nearly 30 points in the first 30 minutes of trade to 12,359.98 on heavy turnover of HK$1.18 billion.
"Momentum is the most important thing and turnover, like yesterday's around HK$7 billion, is boosting momentum," said Lai.
"The Hong Kong market is quite overbought but continues to follow the Dow Jones," said Calvin Chan, technical analyst at NAVA SC Securities.
The index has tried to consolidate in recent days, but keeps getting a new boost from the bullish trend on Wall Street, Chan said.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average closed above 6,000 for the first time at 6,010 on Monday, a gain of 40.62 points.
Earlier on Monday, the Hang Seng Index closed at a new record high of 12,330.35. Hong Kong shares also edged up in overnight trading in London, led by HSBC and Hang Seng Bank.
The commercial and industrial sector led the market in early trade, followed by the property sector. Mid-cap issues were also actively sought.
CITIC Pacific advanced to a record high of HK$37.90, before easing to trade up HK$0.30 at HK$37.70.
Hutchison advanced HK$0.50 to HK$53.75, while Wheelock put on HK$0.25 to trade at HK$17.45, matching its record high. Swire edged up HK$0.25 to HK$71.00.
Sun Hung Kai Properties moved to a new high of HK$87.50 in early trading before easing to trade up HK$0.50 at HK$87.25.
Cheung Kong also continued its rally, gaining HK$1.25 to HK$62.25. Laggard Henderson Investment also struck at new high at HK$8.95 before easing to trade unchanged at HK8.80.

Banking giant HSBC continued its strong performance, hitting a new high of HK$151.00 before easing to trade up HK$1.00 at HK$150.50. Hang Seng Bank also advanced HK$0.75 to trade at a new high of HK$91.00.
